name: FREQUENT FLYWAYS
notes: Was 41: the $400 Canada goose row was a near-verbatim twin of n1-animals' FREQUENT FLYERS $200 and far too easy for R2; replaced with the monarch's multi-generation relay. Hummingbird answer still echoes e1-home (different pack, different angle).

name: COMMUTING WITH NATURE
notes: Serengeti wildebeest, gray whale round trip, Christmas Island red crabs, Porcupine caribou herd, zooplankton vertical migration all verified.

name: PALEO DIET
notes: Permafrost mammoths, La Brea Smilodon, megalodon teeth, trilobites' 250M+ year run to the Great Dying, Dimetrodon as a synapsid — all correct.

name: THE LATE GREATS
notes: Was 42: the $400 dodo row duplicated n1-animals' FLIGHT RISKS anchor; cut it, shifted thylacine/pigeon/auk/sea cow down a rung and added the quagga (Amsterdam, 1883) at $2000.

name: STRANGE BEDFELLOWS
notes: Clownfish kept here as the canonical symbiosis (its n1 twin was removed); oxpecker, honeyguide, goby/pistol shrimp and fig wasp all accurate.

name: YOU SCRATCH MY BACK
notes: Remora, lichen, ant-tended aphids, cleaner wrasse, mycorrhizae all correct; loses repeat points as the file's second symbiosis category.

name: ANIMAL ESP
notes: Echolocation, pit-organ infrared, ampullae of Lorenzini, magnetoreception (properly hedged with 'perhaps'), star-nosed mole's 22 rays — all verified.

name: THE BETTER TO SEE YOU WITH
notes: Was 42: the $400 owl row made 'owl' the third such answer in the Fresh pack and collided with n2-mix in the same round; replaced with the dragonfly's 30,000-lens compound eyes.

name: BIOME, SWEET BIOME
notes: Tundra, savanna, taiga as largest land biome, chaparral, cloud forest all correct; the 'chaps' etymology hands the $1600 answer, but it is a deliberate word-origin hint.

name: LIQUID ASSETS
notes: Reef polyps, mangrove prop roots, Chesapeake as largest U.S. estuary, kelp's 2-feet-a-day growth, hydrothermal vent chemosynthesis — all sound.

name: PET PROJECTS
notes: Dolly (udder cell, 1996, named for Parton), Ham's Jan 1961 flight, Koko and All Ball, Alex's 'none', Clever Hans — all verified.

name: CLAWS CÉLÈBRES
notes: Punxsutawney Phil, Barnum's Jumbo (1882), Hachiko, Cher Ami and the Lost Battalion, Wojtek at Monte Cassino — all accurate; strong closing ramp.
